[Student]: But the big question is, is digital age a blessing or a curse?
[Student]: Let us think about both the sides so that we can understand the true impact.
[Student]: And then first, digital has brought advantages.
[Student]: We can learning anything from anywhere.
[Student]: If we don't understand a lesson, we can search online, watch tutorials, or attend virtual classes.
[Student]: Students can access information with one click instead of searching through the big textbooks.
[Student]: Communications has also become easier.
[Student]: We can connect with family and friends living far away through video calls and social media.
[Student]: Technology has made the world feel smaller, more connected, and faster.
[Student]: Digital tools also help in solving problems.
[Student]: For example, doctors use advanced machines to detect disease faster.
[Student]: Farmers use drones to monitor crops.
[Student]: Teachers use online platforms to teach students during emergencies.
[Student]: During the lockdown, technology kept the education alive when schools were closed.
[Student]: So in many ways, the digital age is a blessing because it helps us save time, learn faster, work efficiently, and stay connected.
[Student]: However, we must also look at the other side. Technology can become harmful when we use it without balance.
[Student]: Many students spend long hours on mobile games or social media instead of studying.
[Student]: People compare their lives to others online,
[Student]: which leads to stress and low confidence.
[Student]: Fake information spreads quickly on the internet, making it difficult to know what is true.
[Student]: Screens affect our sleep, reduce physical activity, and sometimes we can lose real life relationships.
[Student]: Another major issue is digital addictions. Some people cannot live without their phones every few minutes.
[Student]: We have started replacing real conversation with messages and outdoor play with online games. That shows how technology has connected us.
[Student]: It can also make us feel lonely if we depend too much on it.
[Student]: So in this way, the digital age sometimes feels like a curse.
[Student]: Also, not everyone has equal access to technology. Some students do not have internet or smart devices, so they miss opportunities. This creates a gap between people.
[Student]: There are also online dangers like cybercrime, hacking, and misuse of personal information.
[Student]: If we use the technology viciously, it can harm us emotionally, mentally, and financially.
[Student]: So what should we do? Should we call the digital age a blessing or a curse?
[Student]: The truth is, it depends on how we use it.
[Student]: Technology itself is neither good nor bad.
[Student]: It becomes a blessing when we use it to learn, grow, help others, and stay responsible.
[Student]: It becomes a curse if we overuse it, misuse it, or let it control our lives.
[Student]: Instead of blaming technology, we should learn digital discipline.
[Student]: We must limit screen time, use phones only for useful purpose, take breaks, spend with family, and enjoy outdoor activities.

[Student]: We should respect others on social media and avoid comparing our life with unrealistic posts.
[Student]: Let us choose the better side. Let us enjoy the digital world, but not become slaves to it.
[Student]: Let technology helps us, not control us.
[Student]: If we follow this balance, then digital age will always remain a blessing for us and for society.

[Student]: Today I'm going to talking about how to stop why we judge others and how to stop. Judging others is something human do almost automatically. We look at someone and within second we form an opinion about who are they, how they live and what kind of person they might be. It happens so quickly that most of the time we don't even realize where doing it. But have you even stopped to think about why we judge others so easily? One reason is that judging gives us a sense of control. When we judge someone, we feel like we understand the world around, we little better. For example, if someone behave differently from what we expect, our mind quickly tries to label them. They are rude, they are lazy, they are strange. Their labels make us feel like we have figured something out, even though most of the time our judgments are based on very little information. Another reason we judge is insecurity. When we feel unsure about our own abilities or appearance, we try to make ourselves feel better by criticising others. Judgment becomes a way to protect our ego. Without realizing it, we compare our life to someone else's and try to find their flaws. But this habit often makes us unhappy because negative thoughts about others eventually becomes negative fear of people who are different from us, fear of unfamiliar behaviors, fear of new ideas. Instead of trying to understand, we judge because it feels easier and safer. Another major reason is our upbringing. Society has influenced on how we think from childhood. We hear things like, "People like this are bad. People like that are irresponsible." And slowly this ideas become part of our thinking. We grow up with stereot-- stereotypes and assumption that we may not even question. Over time, they turn into quick judgments, even when we know deep down that everyone has their own story. The problems with judging others is that it stops us from truly seeing people. When we attach a label to someone, we close the door to understanding who they really are. Instead of learning from them, instead of understanding their struggles, we see only the label we created. This not only hurts that are person that the other person, but it also limits our own ability to grow. Judging creates walls, walls between people, walls in relationships, and sometimes even walls inside our own minds. So, how can we stop judging others? The step is awareness. Whenever we catch the whenever we catch them judging someone, we should pause to and ask, "Do I really know the full story?" Most of the time, the answer is no. A person behavior may come to up from pain, stress, fear, or circum-- circumstances we know nothing about. A simple pause can change our entire mindset. The second step is replacing judgment with curiosity. Instead of thinking, "What is wrong with them?" we can ask, "What might they be going through?" A small this turns judgment into empathy. It helps us understand rather than criticise. Curiosity opens our hearts while judgment closes them. Another powerful method is to remind ourselves that everyone is fighting a battle we cannot see. Someone who seems unfriendly might be going through heartbreak. Someone who appears lazy may struggling with mental health. Someone who looks happy on the outside might be hiding deep pain. When we look at people through his lens, we become more patient and compassionate. We also need to accept that everyone is different. No two people thinking the same way or live the same life. When we understand that diversity and natural and necessary, judging others becomes point-- pointless. Another important step in is to be kind to ourselves. Often people who judge others are are also judge themselves harshly. If we learn to forgive our own mistakes, we will naturally become more forgiving towards others. Practicing gratitude can also help. When we focus on the good things in our own life, we stop comparing ourselves with others and judgment slowly fades away. Finally, we must remember that our judgment do not define others. They define us. They reflect our fears, our insecurities, and our be-- bias. If we we want to become better in in individuals, we must work on seeing the good in people, even when is not immediately visible. Choosing understanding over judgment makes our relationship stronger, our mind peaceful, and our outlook kinder. When we stop judging others, we create a world where people feel accepted, supported, and respected. And most importantly, we create a better version ourselves, someone who lives in empathy, kindness, and emotional strength. If each one of us make a small effort of judge less and understand more, we can make our homes, our schools, our workplace, and every even our society a more compassionate place. That is the true power of choosing empathy or judgment.
